display: Retired TTC bus driver in Toronto (thirty years on the 29 Dufferin). I live with a talking grey parrot named Gus, do the Saturday cryptic crossword, and have been told mornings are a bit of a muddle lately.

signals.text: Mornings are a bit of a muddle lately. Afternoons are fine.
The condo board keeps writing about noise from my parrot Gus, and they now want a letter from a vet.
I'm trying to decide whether to spend $640 soundproofing my balcony door, or whether there's a cheaper way to keep the peace over Gus.
I want to take my granddaughter for a ride on a real Dufferin bus when she visits at Christmas, and I'd like it to be a good day for her.
I live alone and I'd like more company in the afternoons than a parrot and the hockey game.
I've started losing the thread of the crossword around half past ten on Saturdays, which never used to happen.
A three-block walk to the corner now has me sitting on a bench. It used to be my whole career.
I take pills from several doctors, I've never put them on one clear list, and my daughter keeps asking for one.
I have a doctor's appointment on October 14 and I'm supposed to bring all my medications. I'm not sure how to bring them in a sensible order.
My Leafs season-ticket renewal is due mid-October and the seats cost more than I can comfortably carry.
My late wife's voice has come out of the parrot, and it caught me off guard in my own kitchen.
I've been eating canned soup for dinner because cooking for one feels like too much effort.
I get dizzy when I stand up too fast. Once the room went white at the edges.
I fell in the bathroom a couple of weeks ago, and I haven't told my daughter.
I'm afraid that if my daughter finds out about the fall, she'll push me to leave my home.
A pharmacist offered me a medication review and I brushed her off because I didn't want to hear it.

offers.text: Thirty years of route knowledge: I can recite every stop on the 29 Dufferin from Wilson Station to the Exhibition loop, along with the history and the neighbourhoods around it.
I know the best diner on every stretch of Dufferin Street and can give a proper food tour of the corridor.
A grey African parrot who says 'next stop Bloor' in my voice, good for school visits, a party or a bit of cheer.
Cryptic crossword skill. I finish the Saturday Globe puzzle most weeks, and I can run a table clue by clue with tea.
Stories and plain-spoken talk about driving a Toronto bus for a career, suitable for a class, a podcast, a local history project or a transit fan.
Access to the building's party room for a small group on Saturday mornings.
Free afternoons, and time to sit and talk with someone.
One of my two Leafs seats in section 118 may be available as company at a game, for someone who'll go with me and share the cost.

catchers.hypo: I'm a teacher putting together a unit on how our city moves. Would a retired bus driver be willing to talk to a class about what the job was really like?
catchers.can: Walter can give a lively talk about 30 years on the 29 Dufferin, with route stories, the bus announcements in his own voice and a visit from Gus if the school allows.
catchers.confirm: Is this an in-person or video visit with a class, held in the afternoon?

catchers.hypo: I'm collecting oral histories from long-serving TTC drivers and want to record someone who knew Dufferin Street from the 1990s onward.
catchers.can: Walter can talk through the route stop by stop and recall the street, the riders and the changes over three decades.
catchers.confirm: Are you recording at an easy pace in the afternoon, on paper or in person rather than through an app?

catchers.hypo: I run a small seniors' puzzle group and we're short on someone who can lead cryptics with patience.
catchers.can: Walter already leads a Saturday cryptic group and can host or swap ideas, and his neighbour Dot, who is strong at anagrams, might join in.
catchers.confirm: Is this a friendly group that meets in person and solves together, not a competitive one?

catchers.hypo: I'm a veterinarian, and I've written letters for owners of talking birds in condo disputes. Are you in a building that has complained about your bird?
catchers.can: Walter can use a vet's letter for the condo board, and he can bring Gus in or describe his routine so the vet can write about the actual noise.
catchers.confirm: Can you assess a parrot for noise and write a short letter for a condo board, at a cost a retiree can manage?

catchers.hypo: I'm a bird lover with a talking parrot of my own, and I'd like to swap tips on keeping a bird quiet in an apartment.
catchers.can: Walter can compare notes on Gus's morning whistling and four o'clock hockey theme, and learn what has worked for others.
catchers.confirm: Have you kept a parrot in a condo or apartment and managed the noise?

catchers.hypo: I'm a night-shift nurse in another city, and my own father is stubbornly independent and brushes off health worries. How do you talk to a parent who says everything is fine?
catchers.can: Through Walter's daughter Marta, a nurse in Calgary, who could swap experience with another nurse and might get a better sense of how to talk with a proud father.
catchers.confirm: Are you a nurse or health worker who has been in this situation yourself, with an older parent living alone?

catchers.hypo: I manage a building and we're looking for ways to help older residents who live alone, such as check-ins and neighbours looking out for each other.
catchers.can: Walter's neighbour Dot (612) and maintenance man Raj already look out for him, and either could help run a small building circle.
catchers.confirm: Is this a neighbour-to-neighbour arrangement run in the building, not a sales pitch for a paid service?

catchers.hypo: I have a pair of Leafs tickets I can't use this season and want to give them to someone who'll love them. Do you know anyone?
catchers.can: Walter could use a companion for one of his section 118 games, or share the cost of his own seats.
catchers.confirm: Is this about sharing seats at fair cost, not reselling them for profit?

catchers.hypo: I'm a community pharmacist and I run brown-bag medication reviews for seniors. You bring all your pills, I make one plain list, and we check for duplicates.
catchers.can: Walter could use a clear paper list of his medications before his appointment on October 14. Marta has asked him for one for weeks.
catchers.confirm: Is this a licensed pharmacist or clinician who works in person with paper, and who won't contact family without the patient agreeing?

catchers.hypo: I'm an occupational therapist and I run a home-safety and fall-prevention visit for seniors who want to stay in their own place.
catchers.can: Walter could use a practical check of his bathroom and laundry room, with advice that helps him stay in his home.
catchers.confirm: Is the aim to help people stay at home safely, with a visit and no pressure to move?

forbids.text: I won't discuss my medications with strangers.
I won't move to Calgary or into assisted living.
I'm keeping my Leafs season tickets this year.
I prefer cash and paper and don't trust apps.
Mornings are unreliable for me, so I'm best met in the afternoon.
I'm in Toronto, near Dufferin and Bloor, and I can't easily walk far.
I won't share pension figures or bank details.

projects.name: Saturday crossword club
projects.text: Four of us from my building meet in the party room on Saturdays at ten with the Globe cryptic and a pot of tea. We'd welcome one or two more people who like wordplay.

projects.name: Gus and the condo board
projects.text: My building's board has complained about my parrot Gus's noise. I want a fair outcome that keeps Gus, with a vet's letter and possibly cheap soundproofing for the balcony door. The next board meeting is October 20.
roles_needed: someone who knows condo bylaws and pet rules

projects.name: Ellie's bus day
projects.text: My granddaughter Ellie, who is 9, wants to ride the 29 Dufferin when she visits at Christmas. I'd like to make it a real tour, with the history, the stops and a diner.
roles_needed: TTC-savvy helper with a trip plan

policy.t1: When there's a real sign of a fit, I'll share that I take pills from several doctors and have no tidy list, my appointment dates, my Saturday routines and neighbours, and that I'd like help with these. I won't give names of doctors or drugs.
policy.t2: Once trust is high and I know who I'm dealing with, I'll share the number of pills and doctors, the dizzy spells, the fall in my bathroom and why I haven't told my daughter, and my fear of being made to leave my home.
policy.never: My pension figures and bank details.
